streak_freeze.note: 12 en keys (streakFreeze.*, paywall.benefit.streak.detail, widgets.streak.copy.frozen.*, widgets.streak.a11y.frozen); no ko copy ships, so this is a seed. references/locale-briefs/ko.md '## Idioms and figurative language' proposes the noun '동결' and the passive '동결되다/동결된', including the past form '동결되었습니다' the same brief names, for the frozen-day state line ('Covered by a freeze.'), matching the formal register decided in '## Address and gender'. forbidden is empty: no en key or Apple ko string reaches for a competing word here (Apple's own ko has no Activity-ring-style 'freeze' vocabulary in the harvest), so there is nothing evidenced to ban yet. Whether '동결' itself reads first as a financial account freeze to an ordinary Korean reader, rather than a neutral/playful pause, is an open call needing a native reaction, not corpus evidence: see 'open' entry 'streak_freeze_connotation' below.

time_value_disclaimer.note: The fixed sentence after a time-value figure, on 11 en keys (achievements.badge.{clockedIn,wageDay,wageHour,wageMonth,wageQuarter,wageWeek,wageYear}.earned, achievements.category.wages.description, widgets.cash.description, widgets.focusRing.a11y.money, widgets.monthlyTimeValue.description). references/locale-briefs/ko.md '## Money frame' fixes this exact form ('번' is the attributive of 벌다, 'to earn', so the sentence reads literally 'not earned money') and says it mirrors this glossary entry exactly. hourly_rate.note: The rate the user sets to price their own time (onboarding.hourlyWage.*, profile.hourlyWage.*, currency.settings.*, screenTimeReport.missingWage, achievements.category.wages.description). '시급' is the ordinary, unambiguous Korean word for 'hourly wage/rate' with no other everyday sense, so it needs no brief passage to justify. '월급'(monthly pay) is forbidden because the en source itself says wage in three places this term governs (onboarding.hourlyWage.title 'Set Your Hourly Wage', .footer 'hourly rate', screenTimeReport.missingWage 'your hourly wage'), which is exactly the word a translator reaches for and exactly wrong, because the app pays nobody. '급여'(salary/pay) is scoped OUT of this ban, not in it: references/locale-briefs/ko.md '## Idioms and figurative language' assigns '급여' as the badge family's own approved category name (achievements.category.payroll.name, 'Payroll'), so banning it catalog-wide would misfire on the app's own shipped copy the moment it ships; word bans here govern only the hourly-rate keys this term names, not every occurrence of the word in the catalog.

daily_focus_goal.note: The daily minutes target drawn as a ring, met or not met (onboarding.dailyFocusGoal.*, profile.focusTarget.*, widgets.focusRing.*). forbidden is empty on purpose: onboarding.personalGoal.* and the quote surfaces legitimately need '목표'-family words for an aspiration, a different sense the concept's own not_this ('aim, aspiration, life goal') keeps separate, so banning the bare noun would fire on correct copy, exactly the reasoning glossary/nl.json gives for 'doel'.

open.recommended_reason: It is the shortest plain Korean noun that fills a one-word widget header and takes a compound ('연속일 위젯'), while running text can still use the fuller phrase '%lld일 연속'; the loanword '스트릭' fails the skill's own rule that a reader without English must understand each line, and '연속 기록' is too long for the tightest header slots.
open.note: No ko copy exists, so all three options are untested against a real render. Keys: widgets.streak.smallHeader, .currentStreakHeader, .displayName, .daysCount, .dayStreakCount, insights.summary.dayStreakTitle, share.card.streakEyebrow, achievements.streak.title, onboarding.welcome.slide.streak.{eyebrow,headline}, paywall.benefit.streak.title, the whole streakFreeze.* family. Evidence per option: '연속일'(consecutive day(s)) is 3 syllables, takes a compound, and Korean nouns do not inflect for number so the same form serves the header regardless of the count (widget_noun.plural_header in apple-coverage shows Apple itself reusing one Korean noun, '위젯', for both 'Widget' and 'Widgets'); '스트릭' is the English loan several Korean gamification apps (Duolingo among them) use, ruled out by the no-English-needed rule; '연속 기록'(consecutive record) is the fullest, most native phrase but at 5 syllables does not fit the tightest widget slots the way '연속일' does. Meanwhile agents write '연속일' in noun/header slots and '%lld일 연속' in running sentences, and list every key that touched the concept; no terms row is added until this closes. Decide before the first ko batch; a flip afterwards is a global term change with its own follow-up batch.

open.recommended_reason: It is what makes the badge family cohere in en, Korean carries the whole workplace vocabulary with ordinary Sino-Korean nouns that have no grammatical gender to manage, and the money frame is already protected by the fixed disclaimers and the banned-word table, not by the badge names.
open.note: Keys: the 24 achievements.badge.*.name values and the 5 achievements.category.*.name values, with their .earned lines. Rule: one conceit per locale, decided once and kept across the family, gender-neutral, with plain descriptors left plain (references/project-context.md '## Content policy'). Evidence per option: keep it draws on Korean employment vocabulary that carries no marked gender at all ('입사'=hired, '재입사'=rehired, '월급제 전환'=salaried/switched to monthly pay, '복귀'=back on shift, '근속'=tenure, '급여'=payroll category, '근무'=shift category) — Korean role nouns are unmarked for gender across the board (references/locale-briefs/ko.md '## Address and gender'), so this family carries none of the Romance-locale agreement risk; drop it replaces the employment names with plain achievement names ('첫 세션', '7일 연속', '50일 완주'), losing the wink but removing any reading of the app as an employer next to a money frame that already says five times that nothing is earned. Salaried maps to '월급제 전환', not the more literal '정규직 전환' (conversion to regular-employee status), because the latter converges semantically on the Tenure badge's own '근속' (continuous service) and the two would read as near-duplicate badges; '월급제 전환' isolates the pay-structure sense instead (references/locale-briefs/ko.md '## Decided conflicts'). Meanwhile the first achievements batch drafts the conceit, marks every name a proposal, and the adjudicator reports the whole family together so a flip is one batch.

open.recommended_reason: It is the more written/formal of the two counters and matches the 하십시오체 register decided for body text throughout the app, while '번' reads slightly more spoken and colloquial.

Both '회' and '번' are ordinary, grammatically correct Korean counters for occurrences; neither is evidenced from the Apple ko harvest in this run (no matching string was captured), so this is a plain register call, not a platform mismatch. Meanwhile agents use '회' consistently across the three keys and record any editor pushback toward '번' in the batch report; a flip is a single find-and-replace across those three keys, not a structural change.

open.recommended_reason: Provisionally: it is the literal, evidenced match for the source 'freeze' concept and reinforces the frost/ice widget treatment, but this needs a native reader's gut reaction, not corpus evidence, before the pilot batch.
open.note: Affects the streak_freeze term above and its 12 governing en keys. '동결' is the standard Korean word for a frozen bank account or frozen assets (계좌 동결, 자산 동결) as well as the neutral verb 'to freeze'; in a money-adjacent app whose money frame already states five times that nothing is earned or lost, a reader's first association with '동결' attached to a wage-tracking feature may be financial rather than playful. No corpus check can settle this either way. Meanwhile agents keep using '동결' and its forms, and the native review recommended in the brief's Identity section is asked explicitly about this word; a flip is a single term-wide rename in this glossary, not a structural change.
